claims.text: The funding opportunity offers capital grants for new buildings, refurbishments, or equipment.

The minimum capital cost for a project is £50,000.
The minimum shortfall in capital funding required is £25,000.
The usual grant range is £40,000 to £75,000.
Match funding may be required if the project cost is between £50,000 and £80,000.
Projects costing above £80,000 require at least 25% match funding upon Stage 2 application.
The application process involves two stages.
Stage 1 applications are submitted online and require a brief project description, total cost, funding shortfall, proposed timetable, and confirmation of Chief Executive support.
Audited accounts for the past two years are required for Stage 1 applications.
Stage 2 applications are by invitation only.
For Stage 2, at least 25% of capital costs must be raised before submission, unless the project cost is under £80,000.
Necessary planning permission should be in place for Stage 2 applications.
Expert reviewers and panels consider Stage 2 applications.
Organizations that have previously received a grant must wait five years before applying for a different project, unless they are universities or large charities with multiple sites.
Organizations turned down at Stage 1 can submit a new application for a different project at any time.
Organizations turned down at Stage 2 must wait at least one year before submitting a new application for a different project.
The same project will not normally be considered twice.
Round 1 Stage 1 applications open on November 20th at 00:01.
Round 1 Stage 1 application deadline is January 5th at 23:59.
Round 1 Stage 2 application deadline is March 1st at 23:59.
Funding decisions for Round 1 are made in June.
Round 2 Stage 1 applications open on May 14th at 00:01.
Round 2 Stage 1 application deadline is July 1st at 23:59.
Round 2 Stage 2 application deadline is September 1st at 23:59.
Funding decisions for Round 2 are made in December.
If a deadline falls on a weekend, applications received by 9am on the following Monday are accepted.
Projects must be ongoing at the time of a funding decision (June or December) and are not funded retrospectively.
An invitation to Stage 2 remains open for three funding rounds unless otherwise agreed.
Applicants must be registered charities, local authorities, or equivalent organizations.
If applicable, organizations should have at least a ‘Good’ rating from a regulator like CQC or Ofsted.
The applicant and project must be located in the UK.
The funding does not cover the purchase of land or existing buildings.
Grants are not given directly to individuals.
Grants are not provided through conduit organizations.
Overheads, maintenance costs, and VAT are not funded.
Non-specific appeals, endowment funds, and costs associated with meetings, exhibitions, concerts, expeditions, conferences, and lectures are not funded.
Salary costs and running costs (including vehicle fuel and maintenance) are not funded.
Costs for film, websites, or promotional materials are not funded.
Repayment of loans is not funded.
Projects that have already been completed or will be completed by the time of award are not funded.
